course_name_original: Termodinámica Química Aplicada a la Ingeniería
prerequisites: Basic or applied knowledge of Thermodynamics (acquired in Mechanics and Thermodynamics of first year and Thermal Engineering of second year)
Basic knowledge of Chemistry (acquired in Chemistry of first year)
Basic knowledge of Mathematics (especially elementary aspects of differential calculus covered in Calculus of first year)

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge about material and energy balances, biotechnology, mass transfer, separation operations, chemical reaction engineering, reactor design, and valorization and transformation of raw materials and energy resources.

Ability for the design and management of applied experimentation procedures, especially for the determination of thermodynamic and transport properties, and modeling of phenomena and systems in the field of chemical engineering, fluid flow systems, heat transfer, mass transfer operations, chemical reaction kinetics and reactors.
Know the thermodynamic functions as a complete description of a thermodynamic system and apply them to the study of mixtures and chemical reactions.

Systematically deduce any necessary relationship between thermodynamic functions and express it in terms of directly measurable properties, as well as recognize the range of application or validity of such relationships.
Use empirical equations of state and thermodynamic diagrams and tables to estimate the thermodynamic properties of pure fluids and their mixtures.
Calculate or estimate equilibrium compositions between phases and chemical equilibrium in the most common systems in the chemical industry.
Determine the properties that characterize equilibrium systems and determine the relationships between them.
Identify cubic and generalized equations of state.
Choose the most appropriate equation of state for the specific application based on calculation precision and complexity.
Handle phase diagrams and thermodynamic charts.
Determine energy changes associated with processes.
Establish functional relationships between all thermodynamic variables.
Calculate the thermodynamic properties of real substances using equations of state and generalized correlations.
Calculate molar volumes of any pure compound.
Identify properties of pure compounds, compounds in multicomponent systems, and phases.
Identify properties of the liquid phase and the vapor phase.
Understand the laws governing solutions and their applications.
Calculate equilibrium compositions of binary biphasic systems applying the modified Raoult's law.
Develop expressions to estimate phase compositions at equilibrium.
Describe the procedure to obtain the expression for the equilibrium constant in reacting systems as a function of temperature.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: The scope of Chemical Thermodynamics in Engineering. Review of Thermodynamics: systems, walls, and thermodynamic variables. Differential and integral calculus. Reversible and irreversible processes. First Principle of Thermodynamics: Internal Energy, Work, and Heat. Second Principle of Thermodynamics: Entropy. The state functions H, A, and G.
PVT properties of fluids: Diagrams and equations of state for pure gases and liquids. Equations of state for gas mixtures. Estimation of PVT properties.

Thermodynamic properties of pure fluids: Thermodynamic functions and relationships. Calculation of variations of state functions. Fugacity. Residual properties. Diagrams, tables, and estimation of thermodynamic properties.

Thermodynamic properties in multicomponent systems of variable composition: Fundamental thermodynamic relationships. Chemical potential and phase equilibrium condition. Partial molar properties. Mixture magnitudes. Estimation of thermodynamic properties: ideal gas mixtures, fugacity and fugacity coefficient of a mixed fluid. Ideal solutions and real solutions: activity and activity coefficient. Excess properties.

Thermodynamics of phase equilibrium in solutions: Simple models for phase equilibrium. Estimation of properties in liquid-vapor (L-V) equilibrium (fugacity, activity, excess properties, mixture properties). Complex models for liquid-vapor (L-V) equilibrium. Liquid-liquid (L-L) equilibrium.

Thermodynamics of chemical reaction: Thermochemistry. Extent of reaction. Equilibrium condition. The equilibrium constant and Gibbs energy. Effect of temperature on the equilibrium constant. Relationship of the equilibrium constant with composition. Phase rule and Duhem's theorem for systems with reactions. Equilibrium in multiple reactions.
teaching_methods: Problem solving (in small groups during expository classes, individually/collectively in classroom practice, in groups for tutorials)

assessment_methods.method: Written exams with questions and problems (Partial 1 and Partial 2, or Final Exam)
Exercises at the end of some Classroom Practice (PA) sessions
Team exercises prepared in small groups and presented in group tutorial (TG) sessions

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated either via partial exams (0.35x(Partial 1 + Partial 2) + 0.1xPA + 0.1xENT + 0.1xTG) or via a final exam (0.7xF + 0.1xPA + 0.1xENT + 0.1xTG). A minimum of 4 out of 10 is required for each partial exam (Partial 1 and Partial 2) or the final exam (F) to pass by that route. The final grade must be at least 5.0; otherwise, the qualification will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For extraordinary calls and differentiated evaluation, a single written final exam covering all material will be administered, with a weight of 100%.
